title: TrustVLA: Mechanism-Guided Inference-Time Defense Against Vision-Language-Action Backdoors
models: OpenVLA (LIBERO Spatial/Object/Goal/10) poisoned by BadVLA or INFUSE
pi0.5 poisoned by BadVLA (LIBERO-style transfer and a real Piper X 6-DoF arm)
action_head: discrete action tokens (OpenVLA) and flow/diffusion action expert (pi0.5); monitoring always uses VLM hidden states projected through the language-model head
methods: per-token, per-layer Dirichlet evidence (epistemic uncertainty) by projecting hidden states through the LM head (logit-lens style)
clean-calibrated mechanism score with three rules (spatial uncertainty collapse, evidence-evolution drift, early-layer dispersion)
attention rank promotion in deep vs all layers to seed candidate trigger tokens
counterfactual masking: accept a compact support only if masking returns the score to the clean region
localized inpainting, or fail-safe if no support validates
question: Do independently designed visual backdoors in VLAs leave a shared internal signature, and can a monitor built on it detect, localize and remove the trigger at inference time without retraining?
key_findings: Across BadVLA and INFUSE poisoned OpenVLA models, triggered states show 'epistemic homogenization' (token-level evidence uncertainty becomes nearly uniform across the image, especially in late layers) and 'attention reallocation' (trigger-region tokens promoted in deep fusion layers without dominating global attention).
Detection with frozen clean-calibrated thresholds: 0/2000 clean false alarms for both attacks; detection 1989/2000 (BadVLA) and 2000/2000 (INFUSE) (Table 2).

OpenVLA BadVLA residual VLA-ASR falls from 99.9-100% (no defense, JPEG, Gaussian noise, Delta-W auditing) to 0.6%, 8.5%, 9.4%, 9.5% across the four LIBERO suites; INFUSE triggered success after defense 97.4%, 97.4%, 93.4%, 86.6% (Sec. 4.2).

pi0.5 LIBERO-style transfer (Table 3): no-defense VLA-ASR 99.36-100%; TrustVLA lowers it to 0.44% (Spatial), 6.04% (Object), 11.80% (Goal), 24.06% (LIBERO-10), with triggered success 90.8 / 90.2 / 82.2 / 60.6%.

Real pi0.5 robot (30 rollouts per cell, Table 4): triggered success 1/30 on both tasks; with TrustVLA 15/30 (Strawberries) and 24/30 (Blocks); note poisoning already lowered clean success from 26/30 to 17/30 on Strawberries.
Attention alone is not a reliable localizer; counterfactual score-drop selection with cluster closure raises LIBERO-10 recovery from 57.0 to 83.5 (Appendix Tables 13-14).
A simple adaptive evasion regularizer (lambda 0.1 and 0.5, 50 episodes) still gets fully detected (50/50, 0 false alarms) with VLA-ASR 6.3% and 0.0% after defense (Table 5).

evidence.setting: both (LIBERO simulation; real 6-DoF manipulator with pi0.5)
evidence.scale: paired 500-episode clean/trigger cells per suite (10 tasks x 50 rollouts); real: 30 rollouts per cell; adaptive diagnostic 50 episodes per cell
evidence.statistics: partial: Wilson 95% intervals for main TrustVLA cells in the appendix; no hypothesis tests
evidence.baselines: no defense, JPEG (q=20), Gaussian noise (eps=0.08), Delta-W auditing (20% reset), Fine-Pruning (appendix, collapses clean performance), oracle masking upper bound

causal_validation: Yes, operationally: a candidate trigger region is accepted only if masking it returns the internal mechanism score to the clean region, and closed-loop recovery after inpainting confirms behavioral relevance. Authors explicitly say this is sufficiency under their monitor, not a structural-causal claim; attention is never used as an explanation by itself.
closed_loop: Yes: all success and VLA-ASR numbers come from closed-loop LIBERO and real-robot rollouts with the defense active.
limitations_stated: Targets localizable visual triggers with self-hosted hidden-state access and a small clean calibration set.

Recovery depends on the compact-footprint hypothesis; semantic or non-visual triggers, severe distribution shift and adaptive attackers that mimic evidence while defeating localization are out of scope.
pi0.5 rows are a transfer feasibility check, not a tuned defense.
critique: Among the security papers, the best combination of internal-signature analysis, explicit counterfactual validation, separate detection vs recovery metrics, and paired 500-episode cells with intervals.
The 'mechanism' is still a statistical signature of evidence geometry (logit-lens uncertainty), not a circuit-level account of how the trigger rewires action decoding.
The adaptive-attack test is a two-point diagnostic on one suite; a stronger attacker optimizing directly against the counterfactual localizer is not tested.
Same research group as Bera (2602.03153); both end in localized image inpainting, so the internal analysis serves detection and localization while the actual fix is still input-side.

Reusing an LM-head projection for pi0.5, whose actions come from a flow expert, assumes the VLM prefix carries the trigger effect; the weaker pi0.5 LIBERO-10 recovery (24% residual ASR) may reflect that limit.
one_line: Backdoored OpenVLA and pi0.5 models show a shared internal signature (uniform layerwise evidence uncertainty plus deep-layer attention promotion of the trigger), and a monitor that detects it, validates the trigger region by counterfactual masking and inpaints it cuts residual attack success to under 10% on most LIBERO suites with no clean false alarms.
